title: Christoffel–Darboux identity for Krawtchouk polynomials
statement:
Let $n, t$ be natural numbers with $t + 1 \le n$, and let $a, x$ be real numbers with $a \ne x$. Then there is a positive constant $c > 0$ for which the truncated Christoffel–Darboux kernel satisfies
\[
  \Phi_{n,t}(a,x) \;=\; c\,\frac{K_t^{(n)}(a)\,K_{t+1}^{(n)}(x) - K_{t+1}^{(n)}(a)\,K_t^{(n)}(x)}{a - x},
\]
where $K_j^{(n)}$ denotes the $j$-th Krawtchouk polynomial.
hypotheses_covered: existence of a positive constant c > 0
replaced:
For $t + 1 \le n$ and real $a \ne x$ there is a scalar $c > 0$ with
\[
  \Phi_{n,t}(a,x) \;=\; c\,\frac{K_t^{(n)}(a)K_{t+1}^{(n)}(x) - K_{t+1}^{(n)}(a)K_t^{(n)}(x)}{a - x}.
\]
